enisa_single_reporting_platform.question_asked: What does CRA manufacturer reporting through the ENISA Single Reporting Platform oblige or offer, does a body like CSOAI have standing, and is anything open to us?
enisa_single_reporting_platform.what_it_is_verbatim: The online tool developed, operated and maintained by ENISA to enable manufacturers and, once applicable, open-source software stewards to meet their reporting obligations.
enisa_single_reporting_platform.start_date_verbatim: From 11 September 2026, manufacturers are required to submit these mandatory notifications through the SRP.

cra_timeline_verbatim.entry_into_force: The CRA entered into force on 10 December 2024.
cra_timeline_verbatim.reporting_obligations: reporting obligations to apply as of 11 September 2026
cra_timeline_verbatim.main_obligations: The main obligations introduced by the Act will apply from 11 December 2027

enisa_single_reporting_platform.verdict: NOT A CONSULTATION AND NOT AN INPUT ROUTE. It is an obligation channel, not an opportunity.
enisa_single_reporting_platform.who_may_use_it: Manufacturers and (from 11 December 2027) open-source software stewards, acting through Assigned Representatives who need an EU Login account with MFA.
enisa_single_reporting_platform.third_party_standing_verbatim: FAQ 30: If you are not a manufacturer and would like to report a vulnerability or security issue, please contact the relevant national CSIRT directly. Your submission might be marked as 'invalid' in the SRP.
enisa_single_reporting_platform.voluntary_reporting_verbatim: FAQ 27: The platform has not yet implemented the voluntary reporting functionality provided for under Art. 15(1) and (2) of the CRA.
enisa_single_reporting_platform.future_opening: When Art. 15 voluntary reporting is implemented, FAQ 6 says any natural or legal person will be able to voluntarily report vulnerabilities, cyber threats, incidents and near misses. NO DATE IS PUBLISHED for that. This is the only SRP door that could ever open to CSOAI as a third party. Diary it; do not assume it.
enisa_single_reporting_platform.the_obligation_to_check: CSOAI publishes software (npm packages, an MCP server, signing and verification tooling). If any of that is 'placed on the EU market' as a product with digital elements, CSOAI is itself a CRA manufacturer and the Article 14 reporting duty already applies as of 11 September 2026 — six days ago. This is a liability to assess, not an opportunity to file into. Owner/counsel question, flagged here because it was surfaced by this sweep.
enisa_single_reporting_platform.csoai_standing: NONE as a participant. Possible standing as an obligated manufacturer — unresolved.

open_windows.name: NIST AI 200-2 ipd — "The TEVV-Athlon Framework for Evaluating AI Systems"
open_windows.body: NIST ITL AI Program, US Department of Commerce
open_windows.who_may_submit: verbatim: "NIST encourages all stakeholders to provide input, including organizations with experience conducting AI evaluations as well as users of AI evaluation reports - for instance, business decision-makers, procurement specialists, researchers, and technical staff." No nationality restriction.
open_windows.format: email TEVV-Athlon [at] nist.gov with "NIST AI 200-2" in the subject; HTML, ASCII, Word, RTF, Excel or PDF attachments
open_windows.csoai_standing: BEST FIT IN THIS SWEEP. NIST's question 1 asks about definitions and usage of testing/evaluation/validation/verification terminology, and question 5 about elements warranting clarification, revision, removal or expansion. A TEVV framework produces assessment records; it says nothing today about whether those records are signed, content-addressed, recomputable, or whether corrections propagate. We are literally, in NIST's own words, a 'user of AI evaluation reports'. Email route, no account, no fee, no nationality bar.
questions_nist_asks: Definitions and usage of testing, evaluation, validation and verification (TEVV) and related measurement terminology
The framework's flexibility, scope, and applicability across AI TEVV contexts
AI TEVV processes potentially underaddressed by the current framework
The framework's utility for novel or emerging AI systems
Elements that may warrant clarification, revision, removal, or expansion
Additional concepts, provisions, examples, or supporting materials

best_fit_single_route.name: NIST AI 200-2 ipd — The TEVV-Athlon Framework for Evaluating AI Systems
best_fit_single_route.why: It is the only open window anywhere in this sweep whose subject IS the evaluation of AI systems, it explicitly invites 'users of AI evaluation reports', it asks directly what warrants expansion, it takes email with no account and no fee, and it applies no nationality bar to a UK company. A TEVV framework produces assessment records and says nothing today about whether those records are signed, content-addressed, independently recomputable, or whether corrections propagate to where the numbers travelled. That gap is the whole of what CSOAI measures.
best_fit_single_route.runner_up: NIST RFI on Modernizing the National Vulnerability Database in the Age of AI (closes 2026-10-13, regulations.gov NIST-2026-0100) — its Q3(b) on transparency and auditability of AI-driven prioritization is a direct opening.
best_fit_single_route.standing_door: The NIST Zero Drafts TEVV address (ai-standards+tevvzd@nist.gov) has no deadline at all, and NIST's own shelved-topic list names signed metadata and provenance tracking as a parked topic while inviting input on reprioritisation.
